window.note: THIS END STOPPED WRITING SOMEBODY ELSE'S STORE. validation_store's clear branch now takes the emission when it has no injected trouble device, and writes directly ONLY when the owner itself was handed in by a proof holding the store under a temp root — the one hand that may. It matters here specifically because this module sits on the build inspector's own import path (transitions -> validation_store), so an import of the trouble device here would have put the inspector back on a fire path it must not reach, by a route nobody would think to look at. || THE FINDING THIS VOYAGE OWES A READER IN A YEAR: A BUS DIAL IS A DATABASE DIAL, STATICALLY. cairn/tools/base/bus_client.py reaches denied capability two ways — inference_seam() imports cairn.devices.inference_domain, and _wire() imports bus.bus which imports cairn.devices.db_domain — and build_inspector's own fire_path_unreachable sieve walks the STATIC import graph counting function-local imports as edges, so laziness cannot evade it. Therefore any in-process bus dial statically reaches a database and the inference host, and the build inspector, which must reach neither, CAN NEVER BE A BUS CLIENT. Commit 433cdc9 shipped the chart's 'reconcile clears via the verb' bound and the sieve red it; the bound was not awkward, it was impossible. THE REPLACEMENT IS THE SEAM THE RAISE ALREADY CROSSES: two more emission lanes beside raise_trouble — clear_trouble(identity, by, what_changed) and reconcile_troubles(scope, still, by, what_changed) — each with its own gate name and therefore its own watermark in the drain. Sending is a tool; holding is owned. 433cdc9's ownership reasoning was RIGHT and its conclusion did not follow: what must happen in the owner's hand is the DECIDING and the WRITING, not the ASKING. reconcile is the shape that made it work — a reconciler cannot know what is STALE without READING the store, and both read routes are shut, so it hands the holder the COMPLETE current picture under a scope and the holder clears the rest, moving both halves of the read-modify-write into the one process that owns the JSON. Verdict artifact verdict-20260908T172545-d3f15eb2dd5f.json: 4 of 4 criteria pass, 4 hypotheses confirmed and ONE KILLED — hypothesis 4's 'reconcile clears through the verb', killed by the static measurement above. window.note: a seal snapshots the instance root ONCE per batch and leaves the trail tree empty. MEASURED BEFORE: 2 full copies per proof, 424M and 4.6s apiece = ~848M and ~9.2s of tmpfs (i.e. RAM) before a single tooth ran; a 93-proof re-seal sweep moved ~79G. MEASURED AFTER: 118.0MB disk / 3,619 entries / 0.09s per proof, and the live root read ONCE per process (= per --seal batch). Three changes. (1) The snapshot's ignore hook skips the instance root's own logs/ CONTENTS while keeping the DIRECTORY — 311M of the 424M and ~78,000 of the 81,599 entries, and the two proofs that walk that tree (test_device_logs_unwired, test_instance_seal) were measured correct over an empty one; the test is an ADDRESS match, not a name match, so a deeper logs/ still copies. (2) One pristine snapshot per process, keyed on the live root's top-level name set (the one movement a stale pristine cannot survive, because check_instance_seal refuses a swap missing a live top-level name); each proof's private world is cp -a --reflink=auto from it. (3) ONE copy per proof instead of two: the seal's probe now unlinks its own marker, which buys the same no-contamination guarantee the second 424M copy was buying. Every seal's evidence now carries scratch{measured,bytes,disk_bytes,entries,builds,reuses} — the ticket's watch is that figure and nothing else. 14 teeth in test_isolation.py (6 new), green twice; all 4 new claims falsified in-memory and every tooth BIT. Whole tester component 7/7 green in 42s. TWO FINDINGS AGAINST THE CHART: the survey's '91MB the aider shim's data' is FALSE — it is 91MB of venv the snapshot already skipped by pyvenv.cfg, non-venv data is 84K, so the ro-bind in constrain's bounds saves ~0 bytes and the real saving was the trail tree; and collapsing two swaps to one is in neither constrain's `in` nor its `out`, yet is REQUIRED to reach the falsifier (2 x 118MB = 236MB fails 'under 150MB'). HONEST LIMITS: reflink is a no-op on this box (/ is ext4, /tmp is tmpfs) and is written for the day it is not; and test_isolation still cannot seal under --netns (a nested run_proof inside an outer netns reds), which is unchanged by this build — the committed seal before it was isolation='none' too.

window.note: a seal snapshots the instance root ONCE per batch and leaves the trail tree empty — and the hollow green that fell out of it is fixed here too, by ruling. MEASURED BEFORE, by running HEAD's own snapshot code rather than remembering it: two full copies per sealed proof, 888.7MB / 9.28s / 163,352 entries before a single tooth ran. AFTER, same box same minute: 118.0MB / 0.34s / 3,620 entries for a batch's first proof and 0.09s for every proof after it. Three changes, each with its own tooth: the trail tree arrives EMPTY BUT PRESENT (73% of the bytes, and the DIRECTORY must survive or check_instance_seal reads every later seal INDETERMINATE); the live root is read once per PROCESS, the pristine invalidated on its TOP-LEVEL NAME SET because that is the one movement a stale pristine cannot survive; and ONE copy per proof rather than two, the seal's probe now clearing its own marker. The cost is on the record at every seal — evidence.instance_seal.scratch carries apparent bytes AND disk bytes AND entry count, because the old snapshot was 136MB of content sitting in 424MB of 4KB blocks: apparent alone understates 3x, disk alone hides that the cost is entry COUNT. That IS this ticket's watch, and it now fires on every seal. THE RE-SEAL SWEEP READ 200 PROOFS, 192 GREEN, 8 RED, and attribution was measured rather than argued: the tree was stashed, HEAD confirmed to carry the old two-copy isolation.py, and all 8 re-run there — 7 are red at HEAD too and belong to other tickets. THE EIGHTH WAS A HOLLOW GREEN THE EMPTIER SANDBOX EXPOSED. inference_domain's probe resolved its trail through TWO doors and only the first followed the device: diagnostic_trail() honoured the device's roots and set trail_exists, while a hand-built BreadcrumbLog with no roots supplied the records from the LIVE berth. Its tooth wrote one line into an isolated trail and asserted trail_misses >= 1 — a bound BOTH trails meet — so for two months it passed on the live trail's borrowed lines and never on the line it wrote. The seal did not break that proof; it removed the accident the proof was passing on. FIXED IN THIS VOYAGE BY RULING 2026-09-09-a-bug-the-voyage-uncovers-is-fixed-by-that-voyage (Akien: 'we are just going to attach that to the same ticket as a bug we fix with it'; confirmed 'agreed on all counts. ruled approved and boogied'). The fix is at the BASE CLASS, where the shape cannot come back: DiagnosticBase answered WHERE a device's records are and nothing answered WHAT they are, so the one caller that wanted the lines built its own address and half-followed the device. diagnostic_records() now sits beside diagnostic_trail(), both carrying roots=getattr(self,'_diagnostic_roots',None); inference_domain passes it through; the probe builds no address of its own; the tooth's bound is == 1. Measured both ways: fixed reads trail_misses=1, reverted reads 3312. Four new teeth in test_device_logs_unwired.py hold it and all bite under mutation. Trouble an-inference-call-probe-reads-two-different-trails cleared through its door. THE BOUNDS MOVED BY RULING AND THE BERTHED CHART PACKETS DID NOT — rewriting constrain's bounds.in afterward would make the record lie about what the chart knew when it was charted; the widening is recorded forward, in the ruling and in the verdict's findings.
